focus: Same 'το να as subject heads the noun phrase' angle already told verbatim-pattern on el-3652/el-3662 – fourth telling of the phenomenon, same angle, exceeds the repetition budget.
-οντας makes an adverbial '-ing' participle that frames the main clause – state that rule plainly; 'opens with movement' is not a rule.
μολονότι is the formal 'although' – contrast it with everyday αν και; drop the bare gloss and the 'indicative' jargon.
Doubled καλά is literally 'well well' and flips to 'barely/properly' – the reduplication is the hook the current gloss buries.
όμως floats – it can open the clause (the card actually has όμως εκείνος ήξερε) or sit after the first word; the tip's cited example inverts the card's real word order.
Pluperfect είχε + αποφασίσει = 'had already decided' is a real insight, but αποφασίσει is not a participle – fix the terminology in plain words.
Vague stylistic label ('free indirect thought'), no reusable grammar rule, and the gloss even mismatches the card's subject gender.
κι ας is literally 'and let' – an opaque colloquial concessive meaning 'even though'; lead with the literal logic instead of the bare gloss.
κολλάω literally means 'stick' – something that 'doesn't stick' doesn't add up; add the literal hook the gloss omits.
μα is a common everyday/emphatic 'but' alongside αλλά – 'poetic' is a register mislabel; fix the claim, keep the anchored example.
λάδι is literally 'oil' – Greek's dead-calm sea is oil where English says glass; state the literal image, which is the whole hook.
θα μπορούσε να υποστηριχθεί has no dummy subject – Greek impersonal passive where English must say 'IT could be argued'; that contrast is the earned insight.
δεδομένου ότι is a frozen genitive 'this being given' – the -ου ending is a fossilized absolute construction, not just a synonym for 'given that'.
The συνεπώς vs κατά συνέπεια register contrast is real and worth keeping, but κατά συνέπεια is cited in Greek script without romanization – romanize both.

ενδεχομένως licenses να + verb in the main clause (ενδεχομένως…να μας εμποδίζει) – the possibility adverb triggers the να form; the current tip glosses 'possibly' and misses the card's actual structure.
προκειμένου να is the formal counterpart of everyday για να – anchor that contrast; the bare 'formal in order to' gloss is dictionary content.
καταρχήν (in principle) vs καταρχάς (first of all) – a pair even native speakers confuse; make the contrast the tip instead of a lone gloss.
λαμβανομένων υπόψη shifts to genitive to agree with the following noun (των περιορισμών) – a formal absolute construction; explain in plain words why the ending changes vs λαμβάνοντας υπόψη.
'Concede then pivot: possibly…but' is a generic discourse pattern English shares – no earned Greek insight; the card's real feature (ενδεχομένως + να) is covered by el-3824.
πρίσμα is literally 'prism' – Greek sees things 'under this prism' where English says 'in this light'; lead with the literal image.
